bib.title: StyleCLIP: Text-Driven Manipulation of StyleGAN Imagery

question: Can a pretrained CLIP model drive text-based semantic manipulation of StyleGAN images without per-attribute manual effort or annotated data?
hypothesis: CLIP's joint embedding supplies enough supervision to find StyleGAN latent edits from text alone; directions in CLIP space that match the same semantic change are roughly collinear.
contributions: Text-guided latent optimization using a CLIP loss
A latent residual mapper trained per text prompt
A method mapping a text prompt to an input-agnostic global direction in StyleGAN style space S, with control of strength and disentanglement

method.summary: Three ways to combine a frozen StyleGAN2 generator with a frozen CLIP: per-image latent optimisation in W+ with a CLIP+L2+ID loss; a per-prompt three-part mapper that outputs a residual in W+; and a global direction in style space S derived from CLIP text embedding differences and per-channel relevance. Real images are inverted with e4e.

datasets.name: CelebA-HQ (test set)
datasets.source: Liu et al. 2015; Karras et al. 2017

datasets.name: LSUN cars, LSUN church, AFHQ dogs/cats/wild

models.name: StyleGAN2
models.init_from: pretrained (FFHQ, LSUN cars, LSUN church); StyleGAN2-ada for AFHQ

models.name: CLIP
models.architecture: image and text encoders, frozen; pretrained on 400 million image-text pairs

models.name: Latent mapper (Mc, Mm, Mf)
models.architecture: three fully-connected networks, each like the StyleGAN mapping network but with 4 layers rather than 8; one per coarse/medium/fine group of W+

models.name: ArcFace
models.architecture: pretrained face-recognition network R used for identity loss

training.objective: Mapper: L(w) = L_CLIP(w) + lambda_L2 ||M_t(w)||_2 + lambda_ID L_ID(w), with L_CLIP = cosine distance in CLIP space between G(w+M_t(w)) and the text t; L_ID = 1 - <R(G(ws)), R(G(w))>. Optimizer method: minimise D_CLIP(G(w),t) + lambda_L2 ||w-ws||_2 + lambda_ID L_ID(w) by gradient descent.
training.hardware: single NVIDIA GTX 1080Ti GPU (times in Table 1)
training.compute: mapper training 10-12h per text prompt; global direction preprocessing 4h

other.optimizer_lambdas: per-edit (lambda_L2, lambda_ID) given in Fig 3, e.g. (0.008, 0.005), (0.004, 0), (0.0025, 0)
other.global_direction_pairs: 100 image pairs to estimate mean relevance
other.note: no optimizer, learning rate, batch size or step count for the mapper is stated

inference.samples: qualitative examples; no sample counts for evaluation except 100 pairs for channel relevance
inference.prompting: Global direction: target attribute text plus neutral class (e.g. 'a sports car' vs 'a car'), averaged over CLIP's 80-template ImageNet prompt bank; normalised difference = delta t

parameters.alpha_manipulation_strength: G(s + alpha*delta_s); Fig 6 uses alpha -6..6, Fig 20 uses -2..2
parameters.beta_threshold: channels with |delta_ic . delta_i| < beta zeroed; Fig 6 beta 0.16, 0.14, 0.11; Fig 20 beta 0.40, 0.30, 0.20
parameters.video_defaults: real faces alpha=3 with beta chosen so k=20 channels active; real cars alpha=3, k=100; generated cats alpha=7, k=100

metrics.name: mean and std of pairwise cosine similarity of mapper manipulation directions
metrics.definition: invert CelebA-HQ test set with e4e, feed through trained mappers, cosine similarity between all pairs of resulting manipulation directions

eval.protocol: Mainly qualitative visual comparison; the only quantitative result is Table 2. Comparison with GANSpace/InterFaceGAN/StyleSpace matches step strength to the same change in classifier logit (classifiers pretrained on CelebA). No user study.

prompts.purpose: example CLIP prompt templates for prompt engineering (from Radford et al.)
prompts.text: a bad photo of a {}; a cropped photo of the {}; a black and white photo of a {}; a painting of a {}

evidence.quote: The parameter values we use for the examples in this paper are λL2 = 0.8, λID = 0.1

results.claim: Time and input-dependence of the three methods on one GTX 1080Ti: optimizer 98 sec inference, mapper 10-12h training and 75 ms inference, global direction 4h preprocessing and 72 ms inference.
results.table: Table 1, rows optimizer/mapper/global dir., columns train time and infer. time
results.note: optimizer row has no training; global direction needs 4h one-time preprocessing

results.claim: Mapper manipulation directions for a given prompt are highly similar across inputs (mean pairwise cosine similarity 0.73-0.84).
results.setup: CelebA-HQ test set inverted with e4e, mappers for Mohawk, Afro, Bob-cut, Curly, Beyonce, Taylor Swift, Surprised, Purple hair
results.table: Table 2, row Mean, columns Mohawk..Purple hair (0.82 0.84 0.82 0.84 0.83 0.77 0.79 0.73)
results.note: Std for Surprised is printed 0.893 (others 0.081-0.145), likely a typo for 0.093

results.claim: Using prompt engineering over 80 templates improves CLIP zero-shot ImageNet accuracy by 3.5% over a single prompt.
results.quote: This process improves zero-shot classiﬁcation accuracy by an additional 3.5% over using a single text prompt.

results.claim: Channel relevance is estimated from 100 image pairs with perturbation alpha = 5.
results.setup: global direction method, style space S
results.quote: In practice, we use 100 image pairs to estimate the mean.

results.claim: Mapper beats global direction for complex, identity-specific edits (Trump); global direction wins for simple common attributes (without wrinkles) with more disentanglement; TediGAN fails on all three.
results.setup: Fig 9 qualitative, FFHQ StyleGAN2, e4e inversions, three attributes
results.quote: We conclude that for complex and speciﬁc attributes (especially those that involve identity), the mapper is able to produce better manipulations.

results.claim: Global direction gives edits visually similar to StyleSpace and less entangled than GANSpace and InterFaceGAN on gender, grey hair, lipstick.
results.quote: Our manipulation is very similar to StyleSpace [50], which only changes the target attribute

results.claim: Three separate mapping networks work better than a single one for multi-level edits such as Donald Trump; dropping Mf gives slightly better hairstyle edits.
results.quote: we ﬁnd that with driving text that requires such changes, e.g. “Donald Trump”, a single mapping network does not yield results that are as effective as those produced with three.

results.claim: Without the identity loss the mapper fails to preserve identity, even with lambda_L2 raised to 1.6.
results.quote: we observe that the mapper fails to preserve the identity, and introduces large changes.

results.claim: Method is deployable on a single commodity GPU, unlike DALL-E (12B parameters, over 24GB at 16-bit).
results.setup: comparison to DALL-E stated in related work
results.note: quote: 'a 12-billion parameter ver-' split by hyphenation in text; DALL-E described as 12-billion parameter version of GPT-3

limits: Relies on pretrained StyleGAN and CLIP: cannot edit outside the generator's domain or in poorly covered regions.
Text prompts mapping to sparsely populated CLIP regions do not yield faithful edits.
Drastic edits in diverse datasets are hard (tiger to wolf fails; tiger to lion works), Fig 24.
Optimizer is sensitive to hyperparameters and slow, so it is excluded from comparisons.
Evaluation is almost entirely qualitative; no user study or metric comparing against baselines.
Mapper and optimizer training hyperparameters (optimizer, lr, batch size, steps) are not given in the paper.
Mapper needs a separate 10-12h training run per prompt.

terms.definition: extended latent space of StyleGAN used by the optimizer and mapper
style space of channel-wise style parameters, better disentangled than W and W+ (Wu et al.)
input-agnostic manipulation direction delta_s in S derived from a text prompt

lineage.note: frozen CLIP provides the loss and the text direction

lineage.quote: We use StyleGAN2 [19] in all our experiments.

lineage.note: global directions are in style space S; also a baseline
